quisque: quisque, quaeque, quidque — each one, everyone (m. nom. sg.)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quoque: quoque (adv.) — also, too (follows the word it stresses) · also quō (adv.), where + -que 'and' (quoque ostendit se, and where she shows herself)
rapit: rapiō, -ere, rapuī, raptum — to seize, snatch, hurry along (3rd sg. pres.)
rara: rārus, -a, -um — thin, loose, wide-meshed, scattered (n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (rara semita)
rebus: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (abl./dat. pl.)
rerum: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (gen. pl.)
rostro: rōstrum, -ī (n.) — beak, ship's beak, prow (abl./dat. sg.)
rutuli: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Rutulians, people of Turnus in Latium (nom. pl.); Rutulus, -ī, a Rutulian (gen. sg.) · also m. voc. pl. (O Rutuli)
rutulos: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Rutulians, Turnus's people in Latium (acc. pl.)
sarpedonis: Sarpedōn, -onis (m.) — Sarpedon, Lycian prince, ally of Troy and son of Jupiter (gen. sg.)
secabat: secō, -āre, -uī, sectum — to cut, cleave (3rd sg. impf.)
secat: secō, -āre, secuī, sectum — to cut, cut off, sever (3rd sg. pres.)
secumque: secum (sē + cum) — with oneself, with himself/herself/themselves + -que 'and'
sedet: sedeō, sedēre, sēdī — to sit (3rd sg. pres.) · also impers., it is fixed, resolved (+ dat.)
senior: senior, -ius — older, aged; senior (m.), an elder, old man (comp. of senex, m. nom. sg.)
sequendi: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue, trace (gerund, gen. sg.)
sequitur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, come after (3rd sg. pres. of deponent)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
seu: seu (sīve) — or if; seu… seu, whether… or
sibi: suī (reflexive pron.) — to/for himself, herself, themselves (dat.)
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
silet: sileō, -ēre, siluī — to be silent, keep quiet (3rd sg. pres.)
sinistris: sinistra, -ae (f.) — left hand (abl. pl.); also sinister, -tra, -trum, left
sit: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
sive: sīve (seu) — or if; sīve… sīve, whether… or
solio: solium, -ī (n.) — throne, seat of state (abl. sg.)
solo: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, floor, soil (abl./dat. sg.) · also sōlus, -a, -um, alone (m./n. abl. sg.: in solo Volcente)
solvo: solvō, -ere, solvī, solūtum — to loosen, release, set free; pay (1st sg. pres.)
spes: spēs, speī (f.) — hope, expectation (nom. sg.; also acc. pl.)
stant: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd pl. pres.)
sternere: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — to strew, lay low, strike down (pres. inf.)
stygii: Stygius, -a, -um — of the Styx, Stygian, infernal (m. nom. pl.) · also m. gen. sg.
sua: suus, -a, -um — his, her, its, their own (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
sublimem: sublīmis, -e — lifted high, aloft (m./f. acc. sg.)
subnectens: subnectō, -ere, -nexuī, -nexum — to bind beneath, fasten under (pres. part., f. nom. sg.)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
surgit: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, arise (3rd sg. pres.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tarchon: Tarchōn, -onis (m.) — Tarchon, Etruscan leader and ally of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
tenet: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd sg. pres.)
tenetur: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, grip, keep (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
tollit: tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise (3rd sg. pres.)
torrentis: torrēns, -entis — rushing, boiling, torrent-like (pres. part. of torreō; m./f. acc. pl., i-stem form; also gen. sg.)
totum: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
tremefacta: tremefaciō, tremefacere, tremefēcī, tremefactum — to make tremble, terrify (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (illa tremefacta, shaken)
tremefecit: tremefaciō, -ere, -fēcī, -factum — to make tremble, shake (3rd sg. perf.)
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
tros: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg. (Tros Anchisiade)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
ulla: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.); with non, no
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent)
vallis: vallēs, -is (f.) — valley (acc. pl., = vallēs; also nom./gen. sg.)
varios: varius, -a, -um — various, diverse, changing (m. acc. pl.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
venturos: veniō, venīre, vēnī, ventum — to come (fut. part. ventūrus, about to come; m. acc. pl.)
vestra: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
veteres: vetus, veteris — old, ancient, long-standing (m./f. nom./acc. pl.)
viderunt: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see (3rd pl. perf. ind. act., = vīdērunt)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
volucrum: volucris, -is (f.) — bird, winged creature (gen. pl., -um for -ium)
volutant: volūtō, -āre — to roll, make roll (3rd pl. pres.)
volutat: volūtō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to roll over, turn over, ponder (3rd sg. pres.)
zephyri: zephyrus, -ī (m.) — west wind, gentle breeze (nom. pl.; Greek loanword, also gen. sg.)
